label: mid original-phase k/m/h/x/t/1 input after early b/g/j/s/f
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (99% of mass), active at positions t=3..6 (peak t=4-5), never at t<2 and almost never in the copy phase. Fires on certain input tokens, mainly k (32% of mass, 8x lift) and m (21%), then h, 1, x, t, with weaker d/y/2. Mostly on the first occurrence of the token (93% of mass). Context matters: the rate rises when the sequence starts with b/g/j/s/f (first_tok b gives 4x lift) or b appears two steps back. Largest activations are k at t=4-5 after prefixes like s g j b or j b u b. A small trickle fires on <DEL>, again after such prefixes. The predicate (k/m/h/x/t/1 at t=3..6 with b/g/j/s/f in the first two positions) gets dev F1 0.47 and mass recall 0.68. Precision stays low because the same tokens in a similar context often do not fire, which suggests a distributed dependence on the hidden state that a simple predicate does not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=5: k, m, h, 1; t=6: k, m, 1, t; t=4: k, m, h, 1) and the first original token (most: b, j, g, s, f, i; least: 2, y, k, 1); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, L=6 & t=7, t=5.
